calls.head: Who blinks first?
calls.body: The Bruins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Wild are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Bruins.
calls.call: The Bruins’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.4% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Wild.

calls.head: Nowhere to hide for Kaprizov
calls.body: At home, the Bruins keep sending Lindholm’s line (Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Khusnutdinov) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Marco Sturm has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Wild’s first line is Kaprizov, Ek and Boldy.
calls.call: The Bruins’ L2 (Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Khusnutdinov) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Wild’s first line, against about 38% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 65% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 38% with no line matching

calls.said: Marco Sturm would send Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Khusnutdinov out against the Wild’s first line again

calls.head: The Wild hunt in packs
calls.body: The Wild hound the puck, but the Bruins sit back. Minnesota is one of the league’s best for forecheck pressure, and Boston is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Wild to win more pucks back deep in the Bruins’ end.
calls.call: The Wild put more forecheck pressure on than the Bruins.

BOS.head: We had Boston as slight underdogs (40%), and it went Minnesota’s way.

MIN.head: We gave Minnesota a 60% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Minnesota picked Jeremy Swayman apart
surprises.body: Swayman allowed 5 goals on 24 shots, worth 2.2 expected goals: 2.8 more than expected, though three of them came off a pass that set up the shooter. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 25 starts.

story.head: The Wild run away from the Bruins
paras: Ryan Hartman opened the scoring for the Wild early in the first. It was a busy second period. Quinn Hughes and Blake Coleman scored just over a minute apart early in the period to stretch the lead to 3-0. Midway through the second, Fraser Minten got the Bruins on the board on the power play, and Marcus Foligno and Tanner Jeannot squared off. Hartman struck again midway through the second to make it 4-1 for the Wild. David Pastrňák cut Minnesota’s lead to 4-2 early in the third, and Danila Yurov pushed the lead to 5-2 a minute and a half later. Yurov struck again into the empty net with less than five minutes left. Brock Faber played his first game of the season, after missing the first 21, and picked up an assist. Coleman finished with a goal and two assists.

The score flatters the Wild: the Bruins had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Bruins win about six in ten. Jesper Wallstedt made the difference in net, stopping 30 of 32. Jeremy Swayman allowed five goals on 24 shots for the Bruins. Wallstedt has won six straight starts.

Charlie McAvoy took three penalties on his own. Nikita Zadorov picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Bruins killed off a two-man advantage that lasted two minutes late in the third. The Wild improved to 15-3-4, tied for first in the NHL in points, while the Bruins fell to 13-6-1, slipping to fourth in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Wild have points in eleven straight games (9-0-2), the longest run in the league right now.
Quinn Hughes has a point in eleven straight games.
The Bruins’ Connor Clifton was back in the lineup after missing five games.
Kirill Kaprizov extended his point streak against Boston to six games.
